prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near concrete floor, parapet, people’s legs, and round mixing bowls from the farther courtyard, vegetation, buildings, and motorcycles below; the person in frames 1–2 is roughly 0.5–1.5 m in front of the wearer, while the courtyard is several metres below and the opposite structures are farther away. The person moves from the upper-left edge toward the centre-left and remains partly outside the top of the view; facing direction and gaze are not recoverable from the visible legs or depth alone. The nearest bowls and parapet edges appear within roughly 0.5–1 m of the wearer, whereas the brick piles in frames 4–5 are about 1–3 m away, with individual bricks mutually adjacent. This map makes foreground/background separation and the drop beyond the parapet clearer than RGB, but its brightness is not metrically calibrated, distant surfaces merge into dark regions, and some object boundaries and thin structures are blurred.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies a person in frames 1–2, located left and then centre-left, plus several round bowls in frames 3 and 5; it therefore makes instance locations and overlap boundaries easier to isolate than RGB. The person is only partially visible and roughly 0.5–1.5 m away, while the detected bowls are roughly 0.5–2 m in front of the wearer; no reliable body orientation or gaze can be inferred because only lower-body masks are present. The person mask overlaps a small skateboard-labelled region near the feet in frame 2, while several orange tool handles near bowls are labelled as carrots; these objects are close to their respective bowls, generally within a few tenths of a metre. The map is unreliable for full layout because it omits the floor, walls, parapet, bricks, motorcycles, vegetation, and the partly visible person at the top of frame 4, and several labels and mask boundaries are visibly incorrect.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains a single partial yellow skeleton only in frame 2, centred on the nearby person’s lower body at roughly 0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer; the other four frames contain no detected pose. The joints indicate bent, asymmetrically positioned legs, with the lower body extending downward and slightly right, but the torso, head, gaze, hands, and complete facing direction are unavailable because most keypoints are missing or outside the view. The detected lower limbs are near the wearer and plausibly within arm’s reach, while the map provides no spatial relation to the bowls, parapet, bricks, or distant courtyard objects because none are represented. Compared with RGB, it makes the estimated joint arrangement visible despite partial occlusion, but the disconnected cluster near the upper leg and the absence of detections in frames 1 and 4 show that it is unreliable for tracking approach, retreat, turning, or hand reach across the sequence.
